name: Paracetamol
used_for: Relieves pain (such as headache, toothache, period pain, aches) and brings down a fever.
how_to_take: Can be taken with or without food. Leave at least 4 hours between doses and take no more than 4 doses in 24 hours. Do not use for more than 3 days unless a doctor says so.
common_side_effects: Side effects are very rare when taken at the right dose
serious_warnings: If you have taken too much, get urgent medical help even if you feel well
Swelling of the face or throat, rash, or trouble breathing (allergic reaction) - get emergency help
avoid: Other medicines that also contain paracetamol (risk of overdose)
Drinking a lot of alcohol

name: Ibuprofen
used_for: Relieves pain, reduces swelling (inflammation) and brings down a fever.
how_to_take: Take with or just after food or a glass of milk to protect your stomach. Swallow tablets with water.
serious_warnings: Black or bloody poo, or vomiting blood (bleeding in the stomach) - get urgent help
Severe stomach pain
Passing much less urine than usual
Swelling of the face or throat, or trouble breathing - get emergency help
avoid: Other NSAID painkillers (such as diclofenac) or aspirin, unless a doctor says so
Drinking a lot of alcohol
Ask a doctor first if you have stomach ulcers, asthma, or heart, kidney or blood pressure problems

name: Diclofenac
used_for: Relieves pain and swelling, for example from joint problems, sprains or injuries.
how_to_take: Take with or just after food. Swallow tablets whole with water. Use the lowest dose for the shortest time.
serious_warnings: Black or bloody poo, or vomiting blood - get urgent help
Chest pain, or sudden weakness on one side of the body - call emergency services
Yellow skin or eyes
Swelling of the face or throat, or trouble breathing - get emergency help
avoid: Other NSAID painkillers (such as ibuprofen) or aspirin, unless a doctor says so
Drinking a lot of alcohol
Ask a doctor first if you have heart disease, high blood pressure, or stomach ulcers

name: Chlorzoxazone
used_for: Relaxes tight muscles and eases muscle spasm and pain, usually along with rest and other treatment.
how_to_take: Take exactly as prescribed. It can make you drowsy, so be careful until you know how it affects you.
serious_warnings: Yellow skin or eyes, dark urine, pain in the upper right of the stomach, unusual tiredness or loss of appetite (possible liver problem) - stop and contact a doctor
Rash or trouble breathing - get emergency help
avoid: Alcohol
Other medicines that make you sleepy
Driving or using machines if you feel drowsy
notes: Urine may turn orange or reddish-purple; this is harmless. Link from memory: confirm it opens the chlorzoxazone page.

name: Serratiopeptidase
notes: No information in trusted sources (not an approved medicine in the UK or US). App should say: limited reliable information is available for this ingredient; please ask your pharmacist or doctor.

name: Metformin
used_for: Lowers blood sugar in type 2 diabetes.
how_to_take: Take with a meal or just after, to reduce stomach upset. Swallow slow-release tablets whole; do not crush or chew them.
serious_warnings: Feeling very weak or tired, muscle pain, fast breathing, or feeling very cold (rare but serious) - get urgent medical help
avoid: Drinking a lot of alcohol
Tell the doctor you take metformin before any scan that uses dye

name: Glimepiride
used_for: Lowers blood sugar in type 2 diabetes by helping your body release more insulin.
how_to_take: Usually taken once a day with breakfast or the first main meal. Do not skip meals after taking it.
serious_warnings: Shaking, sweating, hunger, confusion or a fast heartbeat (low blood sugar) - eat or drink something sugary straight away
If someone with low blood sugar becomes drowsy or unconscious - call emergency services
Skin may burn more easily in the sun
avoid: Skipping or delaying meals
Alcohol, which raises the risk of low blood sugar
Too much sun without protection

name: Amlodipine
used_for: Treats high blood pressure and prevents chest pain caused by heart disease (angina).
how_to_take: Take once a day at the same time, with or without food. Keep taking it even if you feel well.
serious_warnings: Chest pain that is new or getting worse - get urgent help
Yellow skin or eyes
Swelling of the face or throat, or trouble breathing - get emergency help
avoid: Large amounts of grapefruit or grapefruit juice
Stopping suddenly without talking to your doctor

name: Telmisartan
used_for: Treats high blood pressure and helps lower the risk of heart attack and stroke in some people.
how_to_take: Take once a day at the same time, with or without food. Keep taking it even if you feel well.
common_side_effects: Blocked or runny nose, sore throat
serious_warnings: Fainting
Swelling of the face, lips, tongue or throat - get emergency help
Muscle weakness or an irregular heartbeat (possible high potassium)
Must not be used in pregnancy: if you become pregnant, contact your doctor straight away
avoid: Potassium supplements or salt substitutes, unless your doctor agrees
NSAID painkillers such as ibuprofen or diclofenac, unless your doctor agrees

name: Atorvastatin
used_for: Lowers cholesterol and reduces the risk of heart attack and stroke.
how_to_take: Take once a day at the same time, with or without food.
serious_warnings: Unexplained muscle pain, tenderness or weakness - contact a doctor straight away
Yellow skin or eyes
Swelling of the face or throat, or trouble breathing - get emergency help
avoid: Large amounts of grapefruit juice
Drinking a lot of alcohol
Taking it in pregnancy

name: Rosuvastatin
used_for: Lowers cholesterol and reduces the risk of heart attack and stroke.
how_to_take: Take once a day at the same time, with or without food.
serious_warnings: Unexplained muscle pain, tenderness or weakness - contact a doctor straight away
Yellow skin or eyes
Swelling of the face or throat, or trouble breathing - get emergency help
avoid: Indigestion remedies (antacids) within 2 hours of a dose
Drinking a lot of alcohol
Taking it in pregnancy

name: Levothyroxine
used_for: Replaces thyroid hormone when the thyroid gland is underactive.
how_to_take: Take once a day in the morning on an empty stomach, at least 30 minutes before breakfast, tea or coffee. Usually taken for life; do not stop unless your doctor says so.
common_side_effects: Usually none at the right dose
If the dose is too high: fast heartbeat, sweating, feeling shaky, trouble sleeping, weight loss, diarrhoea
serious_warnings: Chest pain or a very fast or irregular heartbeat - get urgent help
Swelling of the face or throat, or trouble breathing - get emergency help
avoid: Calcium or iron supplements and indigestion remedies within 4 hours of your dose
Taking it with coffee, soya or high-fibre food

name: Pantoprazole
used_for: Reduces stomach acid. Treats heartburn, acid reflux and stomach ulcers, and protects the stomach when taking some painkillers.
how_to_take: Take once a day, usually in the morning about 1 hour before a meal. Swallow whole; do not crush or chew.
serious_warnings: Severe or watery diarrhoea that does not stop, especially with fever - contact a doctor
Joint pain with a rash on skin exposed to the sun
Yellow skin or eyes
avoid: Using it for a long time without a doctor reviewing it
Spicy or fatty food and alcohol, which can make symptoms worse

name: Omeprazole
used_for: Reduces stomach acid. Treats heartburn, acid reflux and stomach ulcers.
how_to_take: Take once a day, usually in the morning before food. Swallow capsules whole.
serious_warnings: Severe or watery diarrhoea that does not stop, especially with fever - contact a doctor
Joint pain with a rash on skin exposed to the sun
Yellow skin or eyes
avoid: Using it for a long time without a doctor reviewing it
Spicy or fatty food and alcohol, which can make symptoms worse

name: Esomeprazole
used_for: Reduces stomach acid. Treats heartburn, acid reflux and stomach ulcers.
how_to_take: Take once a day, at least 1 hour before a meal. Swallow capsules whole.
serious_warnings: Severe or watery diarrhoea that does not stop, especially with fever - contact a doctor
Joint pain with a rash on skin exposed to the sun
Yellow skin or eyes
avoid: Using it for a long time without a doctor reviewing it
Spicy or fatty food and alcohol, which can make symptoms worse

name: Domperidone
used_for: Relieves feeling sick (nausea) and being sick (vomiting).
how_to_take: Take before meals. It is usually only for a short time (often no longer than a week).
serious_warnings: A fast or irregular heartbeat, or fainting - get urgent medical help (risk is higher over age 60)
Shaking or movements you cannot control
Swelling of the face or throat, or trouble breathing - get emergency help
avoid: Taking it for longer than prescribed
Some antibiotics and antifungal medicines that affect heart rhythm - ask a pharmacist before combining

name: Famotidine
used_for: Reduces stomach acid. Treats ulcers, acid reflux and heartburn.
how_to_take: Take as prescribed, with or without food. Often taken once a day at bedtime or twice a day.
serious_warnings: Fast or irregular heartbeat - get urgent help
Confusion (more likely in older people or those with kidney problems) - contact a doctor
Swelling of the face or throat, or trouble breathing - get emergency help
avoid: Other heartburn medicines unless your doctor agrees
Alcohol and spicy food, which can make symptoms worse

name: Amoxicillin
used_for: Treats bacterial infections, such as chest, ear, throat, urine and skin infections.
how_to_take: Take doses evenly spaced through the day, with or without food. Finish the whole course even if you feel better.
serious_warnings: Swelling of the face or throat, a widespread rash, or trouble breathing (serious allergic reaction) - get emergency help
Severe or bloody diarrhoea - contact a doctor
Yellow skin or eyes
avoid: Do not take if you are allergic to penicillin - tell your doctor about any allergy

name: Azithromycin
used_for: Treats bacterial infections, such as chest, ear, throat and skin infections.
how_to_take: Usually taken once a day for a short course (often 3 days). Finish the whole course even if you feel better.
serious_warnings: Fast or irregular heartbeat, or fainting - get urgent help
Severe or bloody diarrhoea - contact a doctor
Yellow skin or eyes
Swelling of the face or throat, or trouble breathing - get emergency help
avoid: Indigestion remedies (antacids) within 2 hours of a dose
Tell your doctor if you have heart rhythm problems

name: Cetirizine
used_for: Relieves allergy symptoms such as sneezing, runny nose, itchy watery eyes, and itchy skin rashes or hives.
how_to_take: Take once a day, with or without food.
serious_warnings: Difficulty passing urine - contact a doctor
Swelling of the face or throat, or trouble breathing - get emergency help
avoid: Alcohol, which can make you sleepier
Driving if you feel sleepy
Taking another antihistamine at the same time

name: Levocetirizine
used_for: Relieves allergy symptoms such as sneezing, runny nose, itchy watery eyes, and hives.
how_to_take: Usually taken once a day in the evening, with or without food.
serious_warnings: Difficulty passing urine - contact a doctor
Swelling of the face or throat, or trouble breathing - get emergency help
avoid: Alcohol, which can make you sleepier
Driving if you feel sleepy
Taking cetirizine at the same time (they are very similar)
notes: Link from memory: confirm it opens the levocetirizine page.

name: Aspirin
used_for: Low-dose aspirin helps prevent blood clots, lowering the risk of heart attack and stroke in people at risk.
how_to_take: Take once a day with or just after food. Swallow gastro-resistant tablets whole. Do not stop suddenly without talking to your doctor.
serious_warnings: Black or bloody poo, vomiting blood, or coughing up blood - get urgent help
A sudden severe headache - get emergency help
Wheezing or trouble breathing - get emergency help
avoid: NSAID painkillers such as ibuprofen or diclofenac, unless your doctor agrees
Drinking a lot of alcohol (raises stomach bleeding risk)

name: Vitamin D3 (Colecalciferol)
used_for: Treats and prevents low vitamin D. Vitamin D helps the body absorb calcium for strong bones.
how_to_take: Take as your doctor says. High-strength capsules (such as 60,000 IU) are usually taken weekly or less often, not every day. Taking it with a meal can help absorption.
common_side_effects: Usually none at the right dose
serious_warnings: Feeling or being sick, constipation, being very thirsty, peeing a lot, or confusion (too much vitamin D) - contact a doctor
avoid: Taking more than one vitamin D product at the same time unless your doctor agrees
Taking more than prescribed

name: Calcium (carbonate)
used_for: Supplement for strong bones or low calcium, often combined with vitamin D.
how_to_take: Calcium carbonate is best taken with food. Follow the dose on the pack or from your doctor.
serious_warnings: Feeling sick, constipation, being very thirsty, peeing a lot, or confusion (too much calcium) - contact a doctor
avoid: Thyroid medicine (levothyroxine) within 4 hours
Iron supplements and some antibiotics at the same time - ask a pharmacist about spacing
